title: Champignons à la grecque
subtitle: Mushrooms braised in white wine and olive oil with coriander seeds
excerpt: Button mushrooms braised in a courtbouillon of white wine, olive oil, tomato, coriander seeds, and lemon juice until tender and well-flavoured. Served cold as a French hors d'oeuvre. Despite the name, this is a firmly French preparation.
sourceNotes: Champignons à la grecque is a classic French hors d'oeuvre preparation. Despite its name ('in the Greek style'), it is a firmly established French culinary tradition documented in Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire (1903) and Larousse Gastronomique (1938). The 'à la grecque' term in French cooking refers to a specific court-bouillon method with olive oil, white wine, and coriander seeds, applied to mushrooms, leeks, celery, cauliflower, and other vegetables.

recipe.batchNotes: Scales up well. The mushrooms keep in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made several hours ahead and served cold. Make the day before a dinner party.

glossaryTerms.definition: A French cooking method in which vegetables are braised in a court-bouillon of olive oil, white wine, lemon juice, and coriander seeds, then served cold. Despite the name, it is a French (not Greek) preparation.

content.text: is one of the standard hors d'oeuvres of the French table: a small dish served cold, before or instead of a starter, to accompany drinks or to sit alongside charcuterie and salads. The mushrooms absorb the court-bouillon as they cool, and after a few hours in the fridge they are very well flavoured, aromatic from the coriander seeds, and sharp from the lemon. You can make them the day before and forget about them until you are ready to serve.

items.prepNote: small button mushrooms, wiped clean, left whole or halved if large

content.text: Combine the white wine, olive oil, lemon juice, tomato purée, coriander seeds, bay leaves, peppercorns, thyme, water, and a generous pinch of salt in a saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and stir to coat. Bring back to the boil, then simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until the mushrooms are just tender. Do not let them become soft and waterlogged.

Transfer everything to a bowl or dish. Leave to cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. The mushrooms will absorb most of the court-bouillon as they cool. Serve cold, scattered with chopped parsley.

items.fix: 8 to 10 minutes is enough. They will continue to cook in the residual heat of the court-bouillon as they cool.

items.cause: Not enough salt, or not enough time marinating
items.fix: Season the court-bouillon generously before adding mushrooms. Leave for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

content.text: The à la grecque method in French cooking has nothing to do with Greece. It is a French preparation that uses olive oil and coriander seeds to give vegetables a Mediterranean character. Escoffier includes versions with leeks, cauliflower, artichoke hearts, and celery. All use the same court-bouillon and are served cold. In a Parisian bistro, they appear as part of the hors d'oeuvres variés, the cold starters before the main meal.
